steps.title: Open Tapeology
steps.narration: Tapeology watches a single US stock and tells you, in plain language, what the order flow is doing right now. We start on the idle home screen, before any ticker is being watched.
steps.point_out: The top bar holds a status dot and a Live / Historical / Simulated source selector; the body invites you to enter a ticker.

steps.title: Type a practice ticker
steps.narration: Simulated mode is selected by default — a deterministic practice feed for trying the read without touching real market data. We type the built-in SIM-BUYER scenario into the ticker box.
steps.point_out: The ticker field now holds SIM-BUYER, ready to watch.

steps.title: Read the practice tape
steps.narration: Press Watch and the single-ticker cockpit comes alive: here the simulated tape is clearly buyer-controlled, shown with a confidence score, a live quote, recent trades, the core flow features, plain-language observations, and an event log.
steps.point_out: The Tape State reads "Buyer Control" with a full confidence bar — the product's plain-language verdict on the order flow.

steps.title: Stop watching
steps.narration: One click on Stop tears the watch down completely and returns to the idle screen — no leftover stream left running in the background.
steps.point_out: We are back to "No ticker watched", a clean slate for the next source.

steps.title: Switch to real historical data
steps.narration: Now to real market data. Historical mode replays a real past trading session through the very same engine — you choose a stock, a date, and a time window.
steps.point_out: New controls appear: a symbol box, a date, a start and end time, and a replay speed.

steps.title: Pick a real stock
steps.narration: We choose Apple (AAPL) — a real, tradable US stock — for the replay.
steps.point_out: The symbol box accepts the real ticker.

steps.title: Choose the session date
steps.narration: We set the date to a recent past trading session.

steps.title: Set the window start
steps.narration: Then a short two-minute window within that session, starting at 15:00.

steps.title: Set the window end
steps.point_out: The replay window is now 15:00 to 15:02.

steps.title: Replay the real session
steps.narration: Press Watch and Apple's real trades and quotes from that window replay through the same engine — same cockpit, same readouts, now driven by genuine market data.
steps.point_out: The source label reads "historical AAPL ..." and the cockpit fills with the real replayed tape; a wide, mixed read honestly shows as "Unclear" rather than a forced call.

steps.title: Go Live
steps.narration: Live mode is where this update lands. Switching to Live shows the real US market session right in the top bar and reveals the live symbol search.
steps.point_out: A "market" status chip shows the real session — open, or closed with the next open time — beside the live symbol search box.

steps.title: Find a stock by search
steps.narration: Start typing and a real symbol search suggests matches as you go — here "AAP" surfaces Apple and its relatives, each with its full company name.
steps.point_out: A live suggestions dropdown lists real matches like "AAPL — Apple Inc. Common Stock".

steps.title: Choose a live ticker
steps.narration: For the live read we pick Ford (F) — a heavily traded name with a tight penny spread, which makes for a clean real-time tape.
steps.point_out: The symbol box now holds F, with Ford Motor Company suggested.

steps.title: Stream Ford live
steps.narration: This is the new capability: press Watch during market hours and Ford's real-time trades and quotes stream straight into the cockpit, with the status dot glowing emerald "live" and the source labelled "live F". Outside market hours it says so honestly, never a fake cockpit.
steps.point_out: An emerald "live" status dot and a "scenario: live F" label over a cockpit fed by the real market — or, off-hours, a plain "Market is closed" message with the next open time.

steps.title: Watch a deliberately quiet feed
steps.narration: To show the honesty guarantee when a live feed goes quiet, we point Live at a deliberately silent test symbol that does not print on the public feed.
steps.point_out: The symbol box holds ZZZQQ, a feed with no incoming trades.

steps.title: Honest "stale" — no invented trades
steps.narration: With no trades arriving, the status dot turns amber and reads "stale" once the quiet passes the configured window — and crucially it invents zero trades to fill the silence, flipping back to "live" only when real data resumes.
steps.point_out: An amber "stale" dot with an empty trade list — proof the product reports a feed gap honestly instead of fabricating activity.
